title: Interleaving maps for adic quotient differentials
statement: Let $k\subseteq F$ be a finite separable extension of fields [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], $A$ a commutative $k$-algebra, and $I\subseteq A$ a finitely generated ideal. Put $C=\varprojlim_{r\ge1}A/I^r$, with canonical map $\iota:A\to C$, and $J=IC$. Fix a $k$-algebra map $\sigma:F\to C$. Put $M=\Omega_{A/k}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], $N=\varprojlim_{r\ge1}M/I^rM$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and let $j:M\to N$ be the canonical map. Give $N$ its componentwise $C$-module structure. Suppose $D:C\to N$ is a $k$-derivation satisfying $D(\iota(a))=j(\mathrm da)$ for $a\in A$ and $D(J^{r+1})\subseteq I^rN$ for every $r\ge1$. Put $B_r=C/J^r=A/I^r$, $Q_r=N/I^rN=M/I^rM$ using the canonical quotient identifications, and $E_r=\Omega_{B_r/F}$, with $F$ acting through $\sigma$. Write $q_r:Q_{r+1}\to Q_r$ for reduction and $t_r:E_{r+1}\to E_r$ for the differential map induced by $B_{r+1}\to B_r$. Then $D\sigma=0$, and the reduction $\delta_r(x)=D(x)\bmod I^rN$ descends to an $F$-derivation $B_{r+1}\to Q_r$. There are unique $C$-linear maps $\alpha_r:Q_r\to E_r$ and $\beta_r:E_{r+1}\to Q_r$ for every $r\ge1$, with scalar actions through the indicated quotients, characterized by $$\alpha_r(\mathrm da\bmod I^rM)=\mathrm d(\iota(a)\bmod J^r),\qquad \beta_r(\mathrm d(x\bmod J^{r+1}))=D(x)\bmod I^rN$$ for all $a\in A$ and $x\in C$. They satisfy, with the displayed domains, $$t_r\alpha_{r+1}=\alpha_rq_r:Q_{r+1}\to E_r,\qquad q_r\beta_{r+1}=\beta_rt_{r+1}:E_{r+2}\to Q_r,$$ $$\beta_r\alpha_{r+1}=q_r:Q_{r+1}\to Q_r,\qquad \alpha_r\beta_r=t_r:E_{r+1}\to E_r.$$

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] to the finitely generated ideal $I$ and to the $A$-modules $A$ and $M$. It gives surjective component projections with kernels $I^rC=J^r$ and $I^rN$, respectively. Thus the stated identifications $B_r=C/J^r=A/I^r$ and $Q_r=N/I^rN=M/I^rM$ are canonical and commute with reduction. They respect the $C$-action: for $c\in C$, $y\in N$, the component of $cy$ at $r$ is $c_ry_r$. The submodule $I^rN$ is $C$-stable since $c(iy)=i(cy)$; hence $J^rN=I^rN$, and the action on $Q_r$ factors through $B_r$. In particular every $x\in C$ has a lift $a\in A$ modulo $J^s$ for any $s\ge1$.

source.place: Tag 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated), both conclusions, with M=A and M=Omega_{A/k}; componentwise multiplication.

proof.text: View $N$ as an $F$-module through $\sigma$. The composite $D\sigma:F\to N$ is additive, vanishes on $k$, and satisfies $D\sigma(fg)=\sigma(f)D\sigma(g)+\sigma(g)D\sigma(f)$, so it is a $k$-derivation. By [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] it factors through $\Omega_{F/k}$, which is zero by [lem-trf-separable-field-differentials-vanish], since $F/k$ is finite separable. Therefore $D\sigma=0$.

For $r\ge1$, the map $a\mapsto\mathrm d(\iota(a)\bmod J^r)$ is a $k$-derivation $A\to E_r$: the map $A\to B_r$ is a $k$-algebra map because $\sigma$ is one. Universality gives an $A$-linear map $M\to E_r$ with these values. Since $I^r$ acts by zero on $E_r$, it kills $I^rM$, and factors uniquely through $Q_r=M/I^rM$. Call the result $\alpha_r$. It is $B_r$-linear, hence $C$-linear, because both module actions factor through $A/I^r=B_r$ and $A\to B_r$ is onto. The symbols $\mathrm da$ generate $M$, so their classes generate $Q_r$ and the formula determines $\alpha_r$ uniquely.

source.place: Tag 00RO (lemma-universal-omega), the symbol presentation preceding Tag 07BK (definition-differentials), and the functorial differential map following 00RO; explicit agent argument for adjacent quotients.

proof.text: The map $x\mapsto D(x)\bmod I^rN$ is a derivation from $C$ into $Q_r$. By the assumed bound on $D(J^{r+1})$, its value is unchanged if $x$ is changed modulo $J^{r+1}$. Thus it descends to an additive map $\delta_r:B_{r+1}\to Q_r$. Its Leibniz rule descends as well, since $J^{r+1}Q_r=0$. Step 2 gives $\delta_r(F)=0$, so it is an $F$-derivation. Universality for $B_{r+1}/F$ gives a unique $B_{r+1}$-linear map $\beta_r:E_{r+1}\to Q_r$ with $\beta_r(\mathrm d(x\bmod J^{r+1}))=D(x)\bmod I^rN$. This is $C$-linear. Every element of $B_{r+1}$ lifts from $C$, so its differential symbols also prove uniqueness for the stated formula.

proof.text: It suffices to check the transition identities on the differential generators, since all maps are $C$-linear. On $\mathrm da\bmod I^{r+1}M$, both $t_r\alpha_{r+1}$ and $\alpha_rq_r$ give $\mathrm d(\iota(a)\bmod J^r)$. On $\mathrm d(x\bmod J^{r+2})$, both $q_r\beta_{r+1}$ and $\beta_rt_{r+1}$ give $D(x)\bmod I^rN$. The generator descriptions follow from the symbol presentation of differentials, and all the reduction maps act on these symbols by reducing their arguments. This proves both transition identities with the displayed domains.

source.place: Tag 00RO (lemma-universal-omega), the symbol presentation preceding Tag 07BK (definition-differentials), and the functorial differential map following 00RO; explicit agent argument for adjacent quotients.

proof.text: On a generator $\mathrm da\bmod I^{r+1}M$ of $Q_{r+1}$, the value of $\beta_r\alpha_{r+1}$ is $D(\iota(a))\bmod I^rN=j(\mathrm da)\bmod I^rN=\mathrm da\bmod I^rM$. The last equality is precisely the canonical projection identification of Step 1. This is also its image under $q_r$. Generation and $C$-linearity give $\beta_r\alpha_{r+1}=q_r$.

source.place: Tag 00RO (lemma-universal-omega), the symbol presentation preceding Tag 07BK (definition-differentials), and the functorial differential map following 00RO; explicit agent argument for adjacent quotients.

proof.text: For a generator $\mathrm d(x\bmod J^{r+1})$ of $E_{r+1}$, choose $a\in A$ lifting $x$ modulo $J^{r+1}$ as in Step 1. The bound on $D$ gives $D(x)-D(\iota(a))\in I^rN$, so $\beta_r$ sends this generator to $\mathrm da\bmod I^rM$. Applying $\alpha_r$ gives $\mathrm d(\iota(a)\bmod J^r)=\mathrm d(x\bmod J^r)$, the value of $t_r$. This checks all generators, including those coming from $C$ outside the image of $A$, and therefore proves $\alpha_r\beta_r=t_r$ by $C$-linearity. Together with Steps 2--6 this establishes every assertion and both uniqueness claims.
